references.text: The command to cover one's nakedness at the altar is linked to the priests' service and holiness before God.
Aaron and his sons receive the priesthood as a perpetual ordinance, as confirmed here as well.
Priests must wash themselves before approaching the altar, or they will die—the same principle of holiness and death penalty for violation.
Nadab and Abihu died because they did not follow God's instructions in the sanctuary service—an example of the consequence of bearing guilt.
Aaron is warned not to enter the Most Holy Place at any time, or he will die—the same theme of approaching God in the right way.
The priests must keep the Lord's commands so as not to incur guilt and death—parallel to the warning in this verse.
The Levites' service at the tabernacle and that they bear their own guilt—linked to the priesthood and its perpetual ordinance.
The priests' entry into the tabernacle and the high priest's entry into the Most Holy Place point forward to Christ's perfect priesthood.
Direct thematic parallel: specific garments as a condition for life when entering the sanctuary.
Theological parallel: closeness to the holy requires specific protection (garments/covering) to avoid death.
Mutual illumination of the principle of death through unlawful nearness to the holy.
Thematic parallel: ritual requirements (garments/washing) as conditions for life when entering the sanctuary.
